Let me analyze this carefully.

The claim: Sen. Lindsey Graham said "President Donald Trump probably knows more about medicine and specifically viruses than the so called scientists at the NIH and CDC".

The retrieved records:

S1: PolitiFact (March 5, 2020) - "Lindsey Graham quote on Trump knowing more about viruses than CDC is fake" - "Sen. Lindsey Graham didn't say that President Trump probably knows more about medicine and viruses than medical professionals. The quote was fabricated by a Twitter account that has posted fake statements in the past." Rated "Pants on Fire" (false and ridiculous). The quote in the Facebook post: "probably knows more about medicine and specifically viruses than any of the so-called scientists at the NIH and CDC."

S2: Newsweek - "That Viral Lindsey Graham Quote Saying Trump Knows More About Viruses Scientists Fake" - "A viral quote attributed to Republican Senator Lindsey Graham is not real. The fake quote... was posted by satirical author Dan Lyons, whose Twitter bio reads, 'aka Fake Steve, inventor of fake news.'"

S3: Reuters - "False claim: Sen. Lindsey Graham said Donald Trump..." - snippet: "Lindsey Graham did not say that President Trump knows more about medicine and science than actual doctors and scientists. Nor did he say that..."

S4: Check Your Fact - "Did Lindsey Graham Say That Trump 'Probably Knows More About Medicine' Than The 'So-Called Scientists At The NIH And CDC'?" - full page but the passages only show the header/byline, not the verdict text. The title suggests it's a fact-check of the claim. Dated 03/17/2020.

S5: Snopes - "Did Sen. Graham Say Trump Knows More Than CDC About Medicine?" - snippet: "U.S. Sen. Lindsey Graham said, 'President Trump probably knows more about medicine and specifically viruses than any of the so-called scientists...'" - This snippet is ambiguous; it appears to quote the claim being checked. Snopes fact-checks typically start with the claim as posted. The snippet alone doesn't show the verdict. But the title "Did Sen. Graham Say Trump Knows More Than CDC About Medicine?" suggests a fact-check. Given the known Snopes rating for this was "False" (actually Snopes rated it "False" — the quote originated from Dan Lyons' satirical tweet). But the retrieved snippet doesn't show the verdict.

So the claim is refuted by multiple fact-checkers: PolitiFact (Pants on Fire), Newsweek, Reuters, and presumably Check Your Fact and Snopes.

The claim as stated: "Sen. Lindsey Graham said 'President Donald Trump probably knows more about medicine and specifically viruses than the so called scientists at the NIH and CDC'."

Note the claim's wording differs slightly from the viral quote: the viral quote says "any of the so-called scientists at the NIH and CDC" and attributes to @LindseyGrahamSC via Dan Lyons' satirical tweet. The claim here says "President Donald Trump probably knows more about medicine and specifically viruses than the so called scientists at the NIH and CDC" — essentially the same fabricated quote.

Verdict: FALSE. The quote is fabricated; Graham never said it. Multiple independent fact-checks (PolitiFact, Reuters, Newsweek) confirm the quote originated from satirical author Dan Lyons.

Confidence: High? The evidence is strong: PolitiFact full page explicitly says Graham didn't say it and the quote was fabricated; Newsweek full page says the quote is not real and was posted by Dan Lyons; Reuters snippet explicitly denies. These are different outlets but may share underlying sourcing (Graham's office statement, Dan Lyons' tweet). Still, the convergence is strong. I'd say High confidence for FALSE.
